chunks: From him, from Sa'dan, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the women of the city (Mecca/Medina). He said: 'They are capable (of marriage).' I asked: 'Should I marry from among them?' He said: 'Yes.' The way to reconcile these two reports, and what follows their pattern, is to consider them as permissible (general allowance), while the earlier reports are considered as indicating excellence and preference (recommendation), and likewise.
ai.seo_question: How to reconcile reports about marrying women of the city in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this report from al-Istibsar, Ali ibn Yaqtin inquires of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the permissibility of marrying the women of Medina, to which the Imam replies affirmatively, describing them as 'fasiq' (virtuous but not necessarily pious). Shia scholars resolve the apparent contradiction with other hadiths by distinguishing between general permissibility (jawaz) and ideal preference (fadl wa istihbab), establishing that while marriage to them is valid, it is not the most recommended choice.
